facts.place: the lake shore on the Vermillion River

entry.description: It means harm, and the old settlers hold that it means harm to one family above all. It is a light of the Dakota prairie, and shows itself as a lantern swinging at the height of a walking man, with no one carrying it, most often in the hour before a blizzard. Its presence is known because there is a jingle of harness, the lamp flame leans toward the door, and the coyotes hush all at once.
entry.first_account: "I saw a lantern coming across the field, swinging like somebody was carrying it. There was nobody carrying it." So a homesteader named Gunhild Tveit reported it in 1893. The explanation given locally is that a section hand named Ole Skjervold was struck by a night train at the lake shore on the Vermillion River while walking the track home from the section house.
entry.precaution: Recommended precaution: The only rule is not to follow it, however near it seems or however familiar.
